tables.comment:
Someone on Verily. Shares its primary key with `auth.accounts`, so deleting
the signed-in account removes this profile.

columns.name: display_name
columns.comment: Display name shown on public action and attempt surfaces.

tables.comment:
A versioned, creator-owned proof contract. Published revisions are
immutable; historical attempts stay tied to the revision they accepted.

columns.name: action_key
columns.comment: Stable key within a creator's catalogue (not globally unique alone).

columns.name: status
columns.comment: `draft`, `published`, `paused`, or `closed`.

columns.name: time_zone
columns.comment: IANA time zone for recurrence windows.

columns.name: place_name
columns.comment: Public place name only — never precise coordinates on the public row.

columns.name: place_radius_meters
columns.comment: Public geofence radius in metres for the place pin, when set.

tables.comment: One account attempt per action period; retries reuse the same attempt.

columns.name: period_key
columns.comment: Recurrence bucket key (for example a calendar day in the action TZ).

columns.name: status
columns.comment:
`collecting_evidence`, `verifying`, `pending_review`, `verified`,
`rejected`, or `capacity_reached`.

columns.name: reward_outcome
columns.comment: Set when a verified attempt met a reward pool: won or why not.

tables.comment:
Private evidence for one requirement on one attempt.

Almost every column is private: evidence originals stay off public feeds.
Policies let only the participant select the row; write paths are server
system transactions in `verily_verification`.

columns.name: requirement_key
columns.comment: Stable key of the requirement this proof satisfies.

columns.name: kind
columns.comment:
Requirement kind: `photo`, `video`, `location`, `motion`, `qr`,
`spoken`, `external`, …

columns.name: sha256_digest
columns.comment: SHA-256 hex of the exact evidence bytes the server accepted.

columns.name: provenance_level
columns.comment: Capture integrity / provenance level label (for example `basic`).

columns.name: capture_key_storage
columns.comment: `strongBox`, `trustedEnvironment`, or `secureEnclave` when attested.

tables.comment:
One escrowed reward pool per creator and action key.

The row id is the on-chain pool id. Terms freeze once funding starts.
Payout indexes are assigned in the DB transaction that verifies an
attempt — never re-indexed on a failed release.

columns.name: mint
columns.comment: SPL mint address (base58).

columns.name: amount_per_payout
columns.comment: Token atoms per verified completion.

columns.name: creator_wallet
columns.comment: Creator wallet frozen when funding starts.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: `draft`, `awaiting_funding`, `funded`, `ended`, or `closed`.

tables.comment:
One per person. Everything else about them, from their emails to their
sessions, points here; the app's own user table shares its key.

columns.name: disabled_at
columns.comment:
When the account was disabled. A disabled account can't sign in, and
its sessions stop working.

columns.name: locked_until
columns.comment: Until when sign-in is refused, after too many failed attempts.

tables.comment:
A short-lived secret a sign-in method sent or expects, such as an email
code or the second step of signing in. Only its hash is stored, it
expires, and it works once.

columns.name: subject
columns.comment: Who it was issued to, such as an email address.

columns.name: state
columns.comment:
What the ceremony needs to finish, such as a WebAuthn challenge or a
PKCE verifier: sealed with the server's keys and bound to this row.

columns.name: attempts
columns.comment: Failed attempts so far.

tables.comment: An email address an account has proved it receives mail at.

columns.name: address
columns.comment: The address, trimmed and lowercased. Each belongs to one account.

columns.name: verified_at
columns.comment: When the account last proved it receives mail here.

columns.name: is_primary
columns.comment: Whether this is the address the account's mail goes to.

tables.comment:
The audit trail: what happened to an account, and from where. Never
credentials.

columns.name: detail
columns.comment:
What it concerns, such as the app that was connected: never a
credential.

tables.comment:
A third-party account someone signs in with, such as their Google
account. Who they are there is the provider and the provider's subject,
never the email address, which some providers let people change to
anything.

columns.name: provider
columns.comment: The provider's ID in `[auth.providers]`, such as `google`.

columns.name: subject
columns.comment: The provider's stable ID for the person.

columns.name: email
columns.comment: The address the provider gave, as it gave it.

columns.name: email_verified
columns.comment:
Whether the provider vouched for that address. Even then, it never
connects accounts by itself.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Their name or username there, to tell connected accounts apart.

columns.name: last_used_at
columns.comment: When it last signed in.

tables.comment:
An account that was merged into another. Old references to it, such as
profile links, resolve to the account that absorbed it.

columns.name: absorbed_id
columns.comment: The account that no longer exists.

columns.name: survivor_id
columns.comment: The account it became part of.

tables.comment:
A passkey: a key pair on the person's device, or synced through their
password manager, whose public half signs them in. Only public keys are
stored.

columns.name: credential_id
columns.comment:
The credential ID the device names the key by. Each belongs to one
account.

columns.name: credential
columns.comment:
The public key, its algorithm, and its signature counter, as
`webauthn-rs` keeps them, in JSON.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: What the person calls it, such as "iCloud Keychain".

columns.name: backed_up
columns.comment:
Whether it's synced to other devices, such as through a password
manager, rather than bound to one.

columns.name: last_used_at
columns.comment: When it last signed in or confirmed it's them.

tables.comment:
An account's password, as an Argon2id hash in the PHC string format,
which names its parameters, so a hash made with older ones is replaced
at the next sign-in. Nobody reads it but this crate.

columns.name: account_id
columns.comment: One password per account.

columns.name: changed_at
columns.comment: When it was last set, changed, or reset.

tables.comment:
A provider's access and refresh tokens for one connected account, kept
only for providers the app configured with `store_tokens`, so the app
can call that provider's API for the person. Both are encrypted with the
server's keys and bound to the identity, so a copy of the database calls
no one's API. Nobody reads them directly, not even their owner: the app
asks [`Auth::provider_access_token`](crate::Auth), which refreshes them.
Disconnecting the account, merging it away, or deleting the account
deletes them, and revokes them where the provider allows.

columns.name: identity_id
columns.comment: The connected account they belong to: one set each.

columns.name: provider
columns.comment: The provider's ID in `[auth.providers]`, such as `github`.

columns.name: access_token
columns.comment: The access token, AES-256-GCM-SIV under the newest key.

columns.name: refresh_token
columns.comment: The refresh token, sealed the same way, when the provider gave one.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: When the access token stops working, if the provider said.

columns.name: scope
columns.comment: The scopes the provider granted, as it listed them.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment: When they were last replaced, at sign-in or by a refresh.

tables.comment:
A fixed-window counter for one action from one source, such as code
requests for one address. The key is a hash, so the table holds no
addresses.

One of an account's recovery codes, for when its authenticator is lost.
Each works once; only its keyed hash is stored.

A signed-in device. The tokens that prove it live only on the device:
this row keeps their SHA-256 hashes, so a copy of the database signs no
one in.

A browser holds one token, in a cookie. A native app holds two: a
short-lived access token it sends with each request, and a refresh token
that trades for a new pair and works once.

columns.name: token_hash
columns.comment: The cookie's token, or a native app's access token.

columns.name: access_expires_at
columns.comment:
When a native app's access token stops working, so it must refresh.
`None` for a browser's cookie.

columns.name: refresh_hash
columns.comment: A native app's refresh token.

columns.name: previous_refresh_hash
columns.comment:
The refresh token this one replaced. Seen again after a short grace,
it means someone else has a copy, and the session ends.

columns.name: refreshed_at
columns.comment: When the refresh token was last replaced.

columns.name: authenticated_at
columns.comment:
When its owner last proved who they are, which carries over when the
session's token is replaced.

columns.name: mfa_at
columns.comment: When its owner last completed a second factor.

columns.name: last_seen_at
columns.comment: When the session was last used, to the minute.

columns.name: idle_expires_at
columns.comment: When it ends unless it's used before then.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: When it ends however often it's used.

columns.name: device
columns.comment: What signed in, such as "Firefox on macOS", for the list of devices.

columns.name: revoked_at
columns.comment: When it was signed out or revoked.

tables.comment:
An account's authenticator app: the TOTP secret it shares with the
server. The secret is encrypted with the server's keys, so a copy of the
database can't produce codes, and bound to its account.

columns.name: account_id
columns.comment: One authenticator per account.

columns.name: secret
columns.comment: AES-256-GCM-SIV under the newest key, with the key's ID.

columns.name: confirmed_at
columns.comment:
When a code from the app first matched. Until then the app isn't
trusted to sign in with.

columns.name: last_used_step
columns.comment: The last 30-second step whose code was used, so no code works twice.

tables.comment:
A wallet linked to an account, with proof that the account's owner
controls it: a Sign-In With Solana message signed by its key. A wallet
belongs to one account. It's private unless its owner shows it, and
signs in only when its owner turns that on.

columns.name: chain
columns.comment: The chain: `solana`.

columns.name: address
columns.comment: The address.

columns.name: label
columns.comment: What the person calls it, such as "Treasury".

columns.name: can_sign_in
columns.comment:
Whether it may sign in to the account. Off until its owner turns it
on.

columns.name: is_public
columns.comment: Whether it shows on its owner's public profile.

columns.name: verified_at
columns.comment: When it was linked.

columns.name: last_proved_at
columns.comment: When it last signed a proof.

columns.name: proof
columns.comment: The latest signed message, kept for audit.

columns.name: proof_signature
columns.comment: The message's signature.

tables.comment:
A `private_key_jwt` assertion an app authenticated with, kept until it
expires so it can't be used twice.

columns.name: jti_hash
columns.comment: The assertion's `jti`, hashed with the client's ID.

tables.comment:
An authorization request: waiting for consent, then an authorization
code, then used. Codes last a minute and work once.

columns.name: id_token_claims
columns.comment: Claims asked for in the ID token with the `claims` parameter.

columns.name: code_challenge
columns.comment: The PKCE `S256` challenge.

columns.name: consent_hash
columns.comment: The handle the consent screen reads it by, while it waits.

columns.name: code_hash
columns.comment: The authorization code, once consent is given.

columns.name: used_at
columns.comment: When it was answered or its code traded.

columns.name: family_id
columns.comment: The family its code started, which a replayed code ends.

tables.comment:
An app that may ask people to sign in with yours. Operators register
them with `lk auth idp client add`; with the developer portal on, people
register their own, which they alone see.

columns.name: client_id
columns.comment: The public identifier the app sends as `client_id`.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The app's name, as the consent screen shows it.

columns.name: secret_hash
columns.comment: The SHA-256 of the client secret, for a confidential client.

columns.name: jwks
columns.comment: The public keys a `private_key_jwt` client signs with, as a JWK set.

columns.name: grant_types
columns.comment: How it gets tokens.

columns.name: id_token_alg
columns.comment: How its ID tokens are signed.

columns.name: redirect_uris
columns.comment: Where codes may be sent, compared exactly.

columns.name: post_logout_redirect_uris
columns.comment: Where people may be sent after signing out, compared exactly.

columns.name: scopes
columns.comment: The scopes the app may ask for.

columns.name: first_party
columns.comment:
One of your own apps: it sees the account ID as `sub` instead of a
pairwise one, and needs no consent.

columns.name: introspection
columns.comment:
Whether it may introspect tokens issued to other apps, as a resource
server does.

columns.name: subject_salt
columns.comment:
Mixed into the pairwise `sub` each account gets for this app, so two
apps can't match up their users.

columns.name: owner_id
columns.comment:
Who registered it in the developer portal; `None` for an app the
operator registered.

columns.name: dpop_bound
columns.comment:
Whether every access token it gets must be bound to a key it holds,
with DPoP (RFC 9449), so a stolen token is useless without the key.

columns.name: registration_hash
columns.comment:
The SHA-256 of the token that manages it, for an app that registered
itself through dynamic registration (RFC 7591 and 7592).

tables.comment:
A sign-in started on a device with no browser, such as a CLI or a TV
(RFC 8628): it shows a short code, someone enters it on their phone or
computer and approves, and the device's polling then gets tokens.

columns.name: device_hash
columns.comment: The secret the device polls with, hashed.

columns.name: user_code_hash
columns.comment: The code people type, hashed.

columns.name: scopes
columns.comment: What the device asked to do.

columns.name: account_id
columns.comment: Who approved or refused it.

columns.name: auth_time
columns.comment: When they last proved who they are, once they approved.

columns.name: approved
columns.comment: Whether they approved, once they answered.

columns.name: interval
columns.comment: Seconds the device must wait between polls.

columns.name: polled_at
columns.comment: When the device last polled.

columns.name: used_at
columns.comment: When the device traded it for tokens.

columns.name: family_id
columns.comment: The family it started, which a replayed device code ends.

tables.comment:
A DPoP proof (RFC 9449) already presented, kept until it's too old to be
accepted anyway, so none works twice.

columns.name: jti_hash
columns.comment: The proof's `jti`, hashed with its key's thumbprint.

tables.comment:
One sign-in of an app: the refresh tokens that descend from one
authorization code or device code. A refresh token presented twice ends
the whole family, since one of the two holders stole it.

An app acting as itself (`client_credentials`) gets a family with no
person, grant or refresh token, so its access tokens can be revoked
too.

columns.name: scopes
columns.comment: The scopes its tokens may carry.

columns.name: id_token_claims
columns.comment:
Claims the app asked to find in its ID tokens with the `claims`
parameter, such as `email`. Only claims its scopes release appear.

columns.name: auth_time
columns.comment: When the person last proved who they are, as `auth_time` says.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: When its refresh tokens stop working however often they're used.

columns.name: revoked_at
columns.comment: When it was revoked, signed out, or ended by a reused token.

columns.name: jkt
columns.comment:
The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the DPoP key its refresh tokens are bound
to, for a public app that started it with a DPoP proof.

tables.comment:
What a person let an app do: the scopes they consented to. One per
account and app; revoking it ends every token the app holds for them.

columns.name: scopes
columns.comment: Every scope they consented to.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment: When they last consented to more.

columns.name: last_used_at
columns.comment: When the app last refreshed its tokens.

tables.comment:
An authorization request an app pushed ahead of sending the browser
(RFC 9126), so its parameters travel server to server rather than
through the address bar. It works once, and soon expires.

columns.name: handle_hash
columns.comment: The `request_uri` handle, hashed.

columns.name: request
columns.comment: The request's parameters.

tables.comment: A refresh token. Only its SHA-256 hash is kept, and it works once.

columns.name: used_at
columns.comment: When it was traded for new tokens.

tables.comment:
A key that signs ID and access tokens. The database keeps only its
public half. An ES256 key's private half is derived from one of the
server's `AUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` whenever it's needed; an RS256 key's is
the RSA key the server was given.

columns.name: kid
columns.comment: The key ID tokens name in their header.

columns.name: derived_from
columns.comment: The ID of the server key an ES256 key is derived from.

columns.name: x
columns.comment: An ES256 key's P-256 coordinates, in base64url.

columns.name: n
columns.comment: An RS256 key's modulus and exponent, in base64url.

columns.name: retires_at
columns.comment: When it stops signing new tokens.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment:
When it leaves the published key set, after every token it signed
has expired.

tables.comment: `live.changes`: one row per written row of a live table.

columns.name: seq
columns.comment: The change's place among the database's changes.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment: The Postgres transaction that wrote it, which joins it to its commit.

columns.name: version
columns.comment: SQLite: the commit's version, set just before the commit.

columns.name: table_name
columns.comment: The changed table, with its namespace: `messages` or `billing.invoices`.

columns.name: op
columns.comment: What the write did.

columns.name: key
columns.comment: The changed row's key, in key column order.

columns.name: old
columns.comment:
The row before an update or delete, without `secret` and
`live = skip` columns.

columns.name: new
columns.comment: The row after an insert or update, without those columns.

columns.name: changed
columns.comment: For an update, every column whose value changed; empty otherwise.

tables.comment:
`live.commits`: one row per committed transaction that wrote a live
table.

columns.name: version
columns.comment:
The transaction's place in the version line. Gaps are transactions
that rolled back after taking a version, which never become visible.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment:
The Postgres transaction ID, which joins the commit to its changes.
`None` on SQLite.

columns.name: committed_at
columns.comment: When the transaction committed.

columns.name: actor
columns.comment: Who made the change, when the transaction said.

columns.name: origin
columns.comment:
What made it: what the transaction said, such as an operation's
name, or `sql`.

columns.name: lsn
columns.comment:
Replication capture: where the commit's record starts in Postgres's
write-ahead log, which orders commits as the database committed them.
`None` for commits captured by triggers.

columns.name: account
columns.comment: Whose notice it is: their account's UUID.

columns.name: action
columns.comment: The button on it.

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: `info`, `success`, `warning`, or `error`.

columns.name: read_at
columns.comment: When its owner read it.

tables.comment:
One enqueued job, in the `rpc` pack's `jobs` table.

It's a live table: a client follows a job with
[`use_job`](crate::client::use_job), and the hub sends each change. Its
policies show a job to the account that enqueued it, and to whoever
`#[rpc::job(visible_to = ...)]` names, and let only the owner change it.

columns.name: key
columns.comment:
The app's idempotency key, if it gave one: enqueuing it again returns
the same job, until the job is pruned.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The job's name.

columns.name: queue
columns.comment: Its queue.

columns.name: arguments
columns.comment: The arguments, as JSON.

columns.name: owner
columns.comment:
The account that enqueued it, as a UUID, or empty when nobody signed
in did.

columns.name: viewer
columns.comment:
Another account that may read it, from `visible_to = argument`, or
empty.

columns.name: visibility
columns.comment: Who else may read it.

columns.name: serial_key
columns.comment:
The job's name and its `serialize_by` argument: at most one job with
a key runs at a time.

columns.name: attempts
columns.comment: How many times a worker has started it.

columns.name: max_attempts
columns.comment: How many starts it gets before it fails.

columns.name: priority
columns.comment: Higher runs first.

columns.name: run_at
columns.comment: Not before this instant.

columns.name: deadline_at
columns.comment: No attempt starts after this instant.

columns.name: started_at
columns.comment: When a worker last started it.

columns.name: finished_at
columns.comment: When it reached `done`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.

columns.name: locked_until
columns.comment: Until when the running worker holds it; `None` when no one does.

columns.name: result
columns.comment: What the body returned, as JSON.

columns.name: error
columns.comment: Why the last attempt failed.

columns.name: progress
columns.comment: What it last said it was doing.

columns.name: fraction
columns.comment: How far along it last said it was, from 0 to 1.

columns.name: steps
columns.comment: The results of the steps it finished, by name.

columns.name: cancel_requested
columns.comment: Someone asked it to stop.

columns.name: failure_pending
columns.comment: It failed, and its `on_failure` mutation hasn't run yet.

tables.comment:
One mutation call that ran with a request ID, and what it returned.

Each caller sees only their own receipts: the policy compares
[`owner`](Self::owner) with the [`ReceiptOwner`] the RPC adds to the
context it runs a mutation in.

columns.name: owner
columns.comment:
Who called: their [`Identity::caller`](super::Identity::caller), such
as a session ID, or [`ANONYMOUS`] for anonymous callers.

columns.name: request_id
columns.comment: The ID the call came with.

columns.name: operation
columns.comment: The operation's name.

columns.name: arguments
columns.comment:
A SHA-256 of the operation's name and arguments, in hex: a repeat
with the same request ID and other arguments is refused rather than
answered with another call's result.

columns.name: result
columns.comment: What the call returned, as JSON.
